quotes.why: The lemma p5 cites, in Haribhadra's own wording and in its own place — the section where he states the treatise's object. Found by direct search.
Dharmamitra names the middling Mother as such, which shows the extensive/middling/condensed nomenclature p5 uses is Indian and not a Tibetan coinage.
The root verse whose 'further three' Haribhadra glosses in terms of the three Mothers. Found by direct search.
Haribhadra reads the root verse's threefold summary as the summary of the three Mothers, which is the strongest textual ground p5 has. Found by direct search.

quotes.text: ལ་ལ་ལས་དོན་གཞན་ལས་ཚིག གཞན་ལས་རྣམ་གྲངས་མིང་གིས་ཏེ། ། མཁས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཡུམ་ཀུན་ལའང་། ། དོན་བསྡུས་དེ་ཙམ་ཤེས་པར་བྱ། ། དེ་ལྟ་མིན་ན་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི། ། རིམ་པ་ལེགས་པར་བསྡུས་མ་ཡིན། ། དེ་ལ་བསྡུས་སོགས་རབ་དབྱེ་བས། ། ཁྱད་པར་ཡོད་པ་ཁོ་ནར་ཟད། །
quotes.why: The verse p5 quotes, with the four lines p5 stops before — which are where the difference among the Mothers is said to be one of extent only. Found by direct search.
The translation colophon: the འགྲེལ་པ p5 appeals to is in Ngok Loden Sherab's revision, which is why p2 singled him out. Found by direct search.
Tsongkhapa glosses the same lemma with the very phrase ཡུམ་རྒྱས་འབྲིང་བསྡུས that opens p5's own position. Found by direct search.
Tsongkhapa glosses p5's ཀྱང and then settles which sūtra the condensed Mother is — a question p5 leaves open. Found by direct search.
Gyaltsab Je's construal of the same lemma: the content is drawn from all three, condensed and extensive alike. Found by direct search.
Gyaltsab rejects the weaker reading of the lemma — 'not contradicting all three' — as self-defeating, which is what p5's use of it presupposes. Found by direct search.
Drepung Loseling glosses the lemma in Gyaltsab's words, so the two houses do not differ here. Found by direct search.
Gomang states the same three-Mother position and derives it from Haribhadra's maṅgala rather than from this lemma. Found by direct search.
